content.user_title: Create Clear Changelogs from Git History
content.value_statement: Technical commit messages make release notes slow and difficult to understand. This skill groups relevant commits and rewrites them as clear, structured changelogs.
actual_capabilities: Analyzes commits from a specified date range or between release references.
Groups changes into features, improvements, fixes, breaking changes, and security updates.
Rewrites technical commit messages in clear, customer-facing language.
Filters internal maintenance such as refactoring and test-only changes.
Applies instructions from a project changelog style guide.
limitations: Requires access to a Git repository and its commit history.
Cannot recover user impact when commit messages lack meaningful context.
Generated classifications and wording require human review before publication.
Does not automatically publish releases or modify repository files.

use_cases.title: Prepare Product Release Notes
use_cases.description: Convert commits for a new version into clear updates organized by user impact.

use_cases.title: Maintain Public Changelogs
use_cases.description: Summarize weekly or monthly development work for a public product updates page.

use_cases.title: Draft Store Update Text
use_cases.description: Turn release commits into concise descriptions for application store submissions.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Changelog
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a changelog from commits since the latest release. Group features, improvements, fixes, breaking changes, and security updates. Exclude internal maintenance.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this for a standard release with no custom format.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize a Date Range
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate customer-facing release notes for commits between {start_date} and {end_date}. Use concise headings and explain user impact.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this for weekly or monthly product updates.

prompt_templates.title: Apply a Style Guide
prompt_templates.prompt: Create release notes from {start_ref} to {end_ref}. Follow {style_file}, preserve required terminology, and flag unclear commits for review.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when the repository defines changelog standards.

prompt_templates.title: Create Audience-Specific Summaries
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze commits between {start_ref} and {end_ref}. Produce separate customer and internal summaries, identify breaking changes, and note uncertain classifications.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this for coordinated releases across product and engineering teams.

output_examples.input: Commits add team workspaces, improve synchronization speed, and fix large image uploads.
output_examples.output: New Features: Create separate team workspaces. Improvements: Files synchronize faster. Fixes: Large images now upload reliably.

output_examples.input: Commits update tests, refactor storage code, and correct notification badge counts.
output_examples.output: Fixes: Notification badges now display the correct count. Internal test and refactoring changes are excluded.

output_examples.input: Commits remove an old API and add a replacement endpoint.
output_examples.output: Breaking Changes: The legacy API was removed. Integrations must migrate to the replacement endpoint before upgrading.

best_practices: Specify exact dates or release references to define the commit range.
Provide a style guide and intended audience before generating release notes.
Verify technical accuracy, user impact, and breaking changes before publication.
anti_patterns: Do not publish generated notes without reviewing ambiguous commit messages.
Do not include every maintenance commit when it offers no user value.
Do not describe performance or security improvements without evidence from the repository.

faq.question: What repository access does this skill need?
faq.answer: It needs read access to the target Git repository and relevant commit history.

faq.question: Can it generate notes between two versions?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the starting and ending release references in the prompt.

faq.question: Can it follow our writing style?
faq.answer: Yes. Reference a changelog style file or include concise voice and formatting requirements.

faq.question: Does it exclude internal development work?
faq.answer: It can omit tests, refactoring, and maintenance commits that do not affect users.

faq.question: Will it publish the changelog automatically?
faq.answer: No. The skill drafts content and expects a person to review and publish it.

faq.question: How does it handle unclear commits?
faq.answer: Ask it to flag uncertain classifications. Review those commits and provide additional issue or pull request context.
